Cover at least one reported usage per shape the rule declares, one alias, and the lookalikes above. A lookalike that the analysis reports is a bug in the rule or the analysis; fix it before the rule merges.

A rule ships with two fixtures, and the harness runs them without any test code:

tests/fixtures/<rule-id>/match/   # a small repository the rule must report
tests/fixtures/<rule-id>/clean/   # a lookalike repository the rule must not report
Both directories are scanned offline as untrusted input, exactly like a repository. The
fixture must observe the rule and
must not. A rule is observed when a detector reports it or, for a rule with
matchers, when the usage analysis finds a match; a rule without both directories fails.

offing rules test <rule-id>          # exits 1 when a fixture fails and prints the expected and actual observations
offing rules lint [file...]          # checks schema, dates, source URLs, and duplicate ids with a fix hint

Keep fixtures tiny and give each one only the files its detector reads. The fixtures are also the reviewable evidence that the detector reports the rule where it should. When the detector changes, update them in the same pull request; when an update of
changes the rule, update them in the pull request that updates it.

Every rule needs an authoritative, versioned source: maintainer release notes, an official support or end-of-life policy, a registry deprecation flag, or platform documentation.
Never infer lifecycle status from popularity, download counts, or a newer version existing.
Dates, affected versions, and replacements must match the source. If the source is ambiguous, say so in the pull request.

- rule "npm.package.left-pad.deprecated": purl must be canonical and version-less (expected "pkg:npm/left-pad")

A tool converts registries written in the older, detector-specific format of the four bundled detectors. It derives
from the old fields, refuses to guess lifecycle events, and checks that every rule reads back unchanged:

npm run build
node dist/tools/registry-v1-to-v2.js registry/example.json \
  --observed-at 2026-10-13 --reviewed-at 2026-10-14 --reviewer your-name \
  --event example.rule.id=deprecated --out registry/example.json
